title: Secrets: environment variables, vaults and what never goes in the repository

videos.script: A key that sends text messages, typed into the code because there was nowhere else to put it that day. {{typed}} The code is pushed. Now everybody who can read the repository has the key. {{pushed}} A secret is any value that grants access by being known. It belongs in one place, and that place is not the code. {{belongs}} The program reads it from its environment when it starts. And if it is missing, the program refuses to start. {{refuse}} Taking the key out of the code is not the end. The history still has it. The fix is a new key. {{rotate}} Today you find a secret before it is committed, move it out, and see why the old copy still matters. {{today}}
